notes.gloss: having more than the average number of accidents
notes.note: Mildly blaming - it turns a count of accidents into a fixed quality, so they seem caused by whatever it describes, not by chance.

notes.gloss: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
notes.note: The sharpest of these: the reachable outcome becomes a thing to hit, so falling short counts as a miss.

notes.gloss: bewildering or striking dumb with wonder
notes.note: The heaviest impact here, falling on the person instead of rating the claim: thrown into confusion or struck silent with wonder.

notes.gloss: liable to a fine
notes.note: As dry as *finable*: a penalty applies, and nothing is said about the wrong or the person who did it.

notes.gloss: filled with melancholy and despondency
notes.note: Gentle and sympathetic, placing the low spirits in the heart and inviting comfort where *grim* rules it out.

notes.gloss: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
notes.note: Faint and formal - it treats falling short of accepted standards as unattractive rather than shocking, staying well back from *indecent*.

notes.gloss: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
notes.note: Not to be shaken, but because it does not bend - the resolve seems unbending as much as strong.

notes.gloss: a disposition free from stress or emotion
notes.note: Soothing rather than lofty: a nature free of stress, praised as restful, where *serenity* raises it higher.

notes.gloss: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
notes.note: Condemns while it defines: a shameful greed for getting things, and a hunger for wealth that nothing can fill.

notes.gloss: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
notes.note: Its *un-* means not a ripple raised, so it hints at water that held its surface, where *smooth* just describes one.

notes.gloss: beyond normal limits
notes.note: Faults the excess for not being justified rather than for its size - the quietest complaint of the words meaning beyond normal limits.

notes.gloss: having particular physiological functions augmented or replaced by electronic or electromechanical components
notes.note: Strictly technical — body functions boosted or replaced by machines, without the sense of lack the other words here attach to made things.

notes.gloss: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
notes.note: Makes the ruin feel bound to happen, as though the outcome were fixed before the event - a heavy seriousness *disastrous* never claims.

notes.gloss: not compatible with other facts
notes.note: Formal and measuring - it notes the mismatch with the facts coolly, where *incompatible* passes judgement on it.

notes.gloss: dried out
notes.note: Names lost moisture, not foulness: a fault of texture, with none of the disgust in *rotten* or *rancid*.

notes.gloss: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
notes.note: Like *blamable*, it shows no personal feeling, treating the wrong, the evil and the merely harmful alike, in one steady tone.

notes.gloss: speaking or spoken fittingly or pleasingly
notes.note: Approves speech that fits the occasion or pleases the ear, where *fluent* asks only that the words come easily.

notes.gloss: not easily borne; wearing
notes.note: The difficulty sits in the thing: a load fixed on you that must be carried, not merely a strain that tires.

notes.gloss: having a silver-colored body
notes.note: The -y ending softens the colour to 'like silver' - a sheen hinted at where *silver-bodied* names the shade outright.

notes.gloss: a defense of some offensive behavior or some failure to keep a promise etc.
notes.note: Admits the fault while covering it - what it defends is already offensive behaviour or a broken promise, where *defence* assumes no wrong.

notes.gloss: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
notes.note: Approving - the strictness comes across as discipline worth having, where *tight* only pinches.

notes.gloss: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
notes.note: Praises by what is missing - nothing foul in the play - where *sportsmanlike* names the good quality directly.

notes.gloss: undesirably noticeable
notes.note: The one word here that judges: as noticeable as it gets, and unwanted, where *marked* only measures how much.

notes.gloss: having a relatively long body
notes.note: Pure measurement in one direction - long compared with other bodies, with no praise or fault in it.

notes.gloss: accept as true
notes.note: Blunt and informal where *believe* is plain: it treats a claim as something on offer, so accepting it sounds weighed, not simply held.

notes.gloss: apathy demonstrated by an absence of emotional reactions
notes.note: The restrained word: it reports only that no emotional reaction came, where *stolidity* sees the same blankness as dullness in the person.

notes.gloss: wanting in physical strength
notes.note: The flat, basic word here: it names missing physical strength and stops, where sharper words add an attitude to it.

notes.gloss: tending to intrude (especially upon privacy)
notes.note: The plain word for the fault: it names the pushing-in itself, without the scorn in *meddlesome*.

notes.gloss: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
notes.note: Praise at full strength, where *lovable* only describes: you cannot help loving it for being naive or like a child.

notes.gloss: a mistake that results from taking one thing to be another
notes.note: Names how it happened - one thing taken for another - which lets the mistake sound explainable rather than someone's fault.

notes.gloss: having a better than even chance of success
notes.note: The only word here where the imbalance is good news: a better than even chance of success, an advantage rather than a fault.

notes.gloss: a female person who plays a significant role (wife or mistress or girlfriend) in the life of a particular man
notes.note: Defines her by her tie to one man, whether wife, mistress or girlfriend: a possessive edge *female* has none of.

notes.gloss: a person's reputation
notes.note: The plainest word for how others see a person, neither good nor bad itself: it takes whatever *character* or disgrace gets attached.

notes.gloss: having or showing appreciation or a favorable critical judgment or opinion
notes.note: Warm rather than cool: it names plain appreciation or a favourable judgment, where *discriminating* says only that the judgment is sharp.

notes.gloss: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
notes.note: The same temporary loss as *mislaid*, but the fault lies in where it ended up, not in setting it down.

notes.gloss: capable of winning favor
notes.note: Measures pleasing by the favour won, not the pleasure given, so it leans away from praising the thing at all, unlike *charming*.

notes.gloss: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
notes.note: The informal word for *broken*, and the casual tone makes the same failure sound offhand rather than serious.

notes.gloss: cheerfully irresponsible
notes.note: Its sing-song rhyme makes the cheer sound silly and disorganized, tipping into criticism where *happy-go-lucky* stays fond.

notes.gloss: determining or having the power to determine an outcome
notes.note: The plain word, covering what settles an outcome and what only has the power to, with no view on how it turns out.

notes.gloss: not efficient or methodical
notes.note: The calmest criticism here: it blames missing method and the wasted effort that follows, picturing no wreckage at all.

notes.gloss: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
notes.note: Formal where *complete* is plain, and it turns having every needed quality into the highest kind of praise.

notes.gloss: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
notes.note: Blunt and accusing: it blames the person for not knowing a field's basics, where *untutored* blames a lack of schooling.

notes.gloss: believe or accept without questioning or challenge
notes.note: Looks down on the believer, not the claim: to swallow something is to accept it without question or challenge.

notes.gloss: of or characteristic of low rank or importance
notes.note: Puts a thing below others and lets that ranking carry the sting, where *humble* names the same low place without ranking it.

notes.gloss: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
notes.note: Credits the social rules as kept, not merely rudeness avoided.

notes.gloss: as found in nature in the elemental form
notes.note: Simply describes: the thing is found in nature already in its elemental form, and no credit is given for that.

notes.gloss: easy to perceive; especially clearly outlined
notes.note: The plain starting point here: something can be told apart, with no claim about how fine or admirable its edge is.

notes.gloss: low or inferior in station or quality
notes.note: Shrinks rather than ranks: the low quality comes across as being unimportant, not as a place on a ladder.

notes.gloss: having a body or a body of a specified kind; often used in combination
notes.note: The neutral base of the set: just a body, or a body of whatever kind the word before it names.

notes.gloss: cause someone to believe an untruth
notes.note: The same planting of a false belief as *deceive*, but seen as breaking the trust that made the believing possible.

notes.gloss: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
notes.note: Points at the mind as the thing being used, in a higher style than *mental*, passing no judgment on the work done.

notes.gloss: aroused to impatience or anger
notes.note: Something landed, and the feeling is the sudden pull back from it, where *irritated* only wears on.

notes.gloss: designed to promote discipline
notes.note: Names correction or punishment in neutral, official language.

notes.gloss: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
notes.note: Neutral: it says only that the person does not belong here, and allows they may belong elsewhere just as normally.

notes.gloss: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
notes.note: The strongest backing here: it calls a plan solid enough to go ahead as things stand, where *workable* says only it will work.

notes.gloss: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
notes.note: A label, not praise: something is proper or legitimate under Muslim law, and the approval is the law's, not the speaker's.

notes.gloss: showing patient and unruffled self-control and restraint under adversity; slow to retaliate or express resentment
notes.note: Patience when provoked, in the most formal word for it.

notes.gloss: not perceived or commented on
notes.note: Formal and abstract, covering both not noticing a thing and saying nothing of it, with the weight on the noticing.

notes.gloss: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
notes.note: An *-er* form used as plain description, which makes it the softest word here: it suggests a scale rather than naming a state.

notes.gloss: quick and energetic
notes.note: Crisp and practical - the pace wins approval for its efficiency alone, with none of the lightness *merry* adds.

notes.gloss: feelings of excessive pride
notes.note: Cuts the pride down to size: the same excess as *conceit*, but a soft self-admiration, faintly ridiculous rather than offensive.

notes.gloss: highly educated; having extensive information or understanding
notes.note: Praises the sheer amount someone knows - everyday and plain, where *learned* is solemn.

notes.gloss: malevolence by virtue of being malicious or spiteful or nasty
notes.note: Ill will that covers plain nastiness as well as a real wish to harm, so it can bite without the threat *malice* carries.

notes.gloss: susceptible to attack
notes.note: The flat, basic word here: it notes that an attack could land, without saying anything is missing or anyone is at fault.

notes.gloss: so surprisingly impressive as to stun or overwhelm
notes.note: A heavier landing than *astonishing* - the surprise is not just noticed, it takes the ground out from under you.

notes.gloss: having a higher rank
notes.note: Means just what it says - higher in rank than another - and implies nothing past the position itself.

notes.gloss: (superlative of ‘good’) having the most positive qualities
notes.note: The highest form itself - it ends the comparison rather than making one.

notes.gloss: the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful
notes.note: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or just useful, without *price*'s claim that the quality is great.

notes.gloss: harmful to living things
notes.note: The plain-spoken one of its three, naming the same damage to living things in everyday language that *deleterious* and *injurious* refuse.

notes.gloss: wild and menacing
notes.note: Holds the same menace as *feral*, but in stiffer, more formal language.

notes.gloss: to an obscene degree
notes.note: The adverb of *obscene*: the heaviest charge in the family: not merely offensive but built to incite indecency or lust, design rather than effect.

notes.gloss: the justification for some act or belief
notes.note: The plain word for justifying an act or belief, saying nothing of whether it succeeds and, unlike *excuse*, assuming no wrong.

notes.gloss: harshness of manner
notes.note: The plain word for the same harshness, felt as a cutting edge in how someone treats you, not *asperity*'s formal verdict on them.

notes.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
notes.note: Puts the fault in being ordinary, not damaged: the thing is found everywhere, where *threadbare* sees it worn thin.

notes.gloss: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
notes.note: The same fault as *giddy*, stated as a quality of the head rather than a mood.

notes.gloss: not perfect; defective or inadequate
notes.note: The plain word for falling short of perfect - it stops there, without *defective*'s suggestion that something inside has gone wrong.

notes.gloss: not able to be supported or defended
notes.note: Moves the fault from what cannot be borne to what cannot be defended: the weakness is the thing's own, not anyone's strain.

notes.gloss: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
notes.note: The informal version of *bad*, looser and more casual about the same felt discomfort.

notes.gloss: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
notes.note: The plain accusation of overstating - past reasonable limits or past the truth - always implying the real size is smaller.

notes.gloss: a lack of caution in practical affairs
notes.note: Names a fault by what is missing - caution not brought to practical matters - where *rashness* accuses someone of charging ahead.

notes.gloss: unable to find your way
notes.note: Only the passing trouble of not finding your way, with no blame in it - unlike the lasting state *stray* describes.

notes.gloss: causing distress or worry or anxiety
notes.note: It stirs a settled mind out of its calm - a lighter, briefer trouble than the unease *disturbing* keeps up.

notes.gloss: devoid of significance or force
notes.note: Takes the air out of a thing, saying only that nothing of weight is there, and leaves the insult to *vacuous*.

notes.gloss: disgrace or shame
notes.note: Names the disgrace or shame as laid at someone's door, so blame is heard in it where *shame* only records the state.

notes.gloss: someone to whom private matters are confided
notes.note: Defines the friend entirely by what you can tell them, so closeness means trusted secrets, not time spent together as with *companion*.

notes.gloss: young and immature
notes.note: Youth felt as softness: being not fully grown is something easily broken, not something admired.

notes.gloss: fanatically patriotic
notes.note: The sharpest word in the group, hearing the extreme patriotism as eagerness to fight rather than just too much enthusiasm.

notes.gloss: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
notes.note: Informal - you are caught in the trouble and cannot step cleanly out, lighter in tone than *unenviable* but no easier to escape.

notes.gloss: smelling like cedar
notes.note: Takes its smell from a wood and names the whole tree, where *balsam-scented* narrows to a resin.

notes.gloss: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
notes.note: A flat word that states the effect and stops, with none of the speaker's own delight that *awesome* shows openly.

notes.gloss: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
notes.note: A practical judgement, not a hope: the thing can be done with what is at hand now, a test *possible* never applies.

notes.gloss: being favorably inclined
notes.note: The mildest here: a leaning in someone's favour, not praise, so nothing has to be shown as it does with *approving*.

notes.gloss: lacking knowledge gained by study often in a particular field
notes.note: A flat report that knowledge was not gained by study, in a field or in general, with none of *ignorant*'s blame.

notes.gloss: exaggeratedly proper
notes.note: The mildest fault here: a sense of what is proper held so tightly it goes stiff, mocked rather than condemned.

notes.gloss: beyond or deviating from the usual or expected
notes.note: Flatly notes that something strays from the usual or expected, with none of *peculiar*'s second look.

notes.gloss: rousing to activity or heightened action as by spurring or goading
notes.note: The one welcome stirring here, though the push behind it keeps an edge of being driven to act rather than persuaded.

notes.gloss: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
notes.note: Of a contest or its contestants, it blames the pairing itself: these two should never have been set against each other.

notes.gloss: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
notes.note: Stresses not caring over staying calm, so the calm looks like something missing, and carries a faint blame that *unconcern* avoids.

notes.gloss: (of persons) taken advantage of
notes.note: Bare and cutting: the word alone reduces the person to a tool, saying far less than *exploited* and landing colder for it.

notes.gloss: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
notes.note: The undignified hurry as a clumsy, messy struggle, where *scamper* is just quick and silly.

notes.gloss: without hope of solution
notes.note: Aimed at the problem, not at anyone: a flat statement that no solution can be hoped for, with no blame in it.

notes.gloss: not affected by jaundice
notes.note: A medical word that says only that jaundice is absent, with none of the approval the other words here carry.

notes.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
notes.note: The softest word here for real physical injury: it carries its lean toward battle lightly and shows nothing of the wound.

notes.gloss: acting like a clown or buffoon
notes.note: Aimed at clowning and playing the fool - silly performance rather than the bad judgement *folly* names, so the disapproval comes with amusement.

notes.gloss: marked by great carelessness
notes.note: The everyday version, mild enough to say to someone's face.

notes.gloss: excellence of manners or social conduct
notes.note: Not just meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it - the highest of these words, where *civility* is the lowest.

notes.gloss: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
notes.note: Openly scornful, not just total - it sneers at the very thing it strengthens, where *complete* only measures it.

notes.gloss: with no effort to conceal
notes.note: Accusing where *bald* is only blunt: not trying to hide it shows nerve, something they should have been ashamed to show.

notes.gloss: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
notes.note: Neutral, covering both a meaning never spelled out and one that sits in a thing's nature, where *unspoken* covers only the first.

notes.gloss: most familiar or renowned
notes.note: Ranks one above all the rest for being known, but claims nothing grander than that first place.

notes.gloss: capable or worthy of being noticed
notes.note: The plain word: able to be noticed or worth noticing, without saying whether that is welcome, which is what *obtrusive* adds.

notes.gloss: an artful or simulated semblance
notes.note: Like *pretence*, a cunning or faked appearance, but pictured as something put on and worn, so the deceit lies in taking it on.

notes.gloss: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
notes.note: Shows disgust rather than disapproval: the thing is so coarse it makes you feel sick, and the word itself is the shudder.

notes.gloss: make conspicuous or noteworthy
notes.note: The only one here that lifts the thing up, making it stand out or worth noticing, where *mark* just labels it.

notes.gloss: quick and energetic
notes.note: More emphasis than description, pushing quickness toward a flat-out rush in a way *brisk* never does.

notes.gloss: a courteous manner that respects accepted social usage
notes.note: The plainest name for behaviour that respects accepted social custom, so mild that the approval barely feels like praise beside *politeness*.

notes.gloss: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
notes.note: The same bruising, but heavy and grim, as if something has gone badly wrong under the skin, where *black-and-blue* stays almost homely.

notes.gloss: rigidly conventional or old-fashioned
notes.note: Flat slang for the same stiff or old-fashioned ways, naming rather than mocking, so it lands softer than *square*.

notes.gloss: spite and resentment at seeing the success of another (personified as one of the deadly sins)
notes.note: Not simply wanting what another has: spite and resentment at their success are the meaning itself.

notes.gloss: doomed to extinction
notes.note: Grave rather than informal: the ending is total and stated with no pleasure in it, where *washed-up* shows scorn.

notes.gloss: very lively and profitable
notes.note: The *-ing* form keeps the gain in motion - still climbing, where *prosperous* names a state already reached.

notes.gloss: causing physical or psychological pain
notes.note: The plain word: it says something hurts, in the body or the mind, without saying how sharply or how much.

notes.gloss: in deplorable condition
notes.note: Wears its awful state on the surface, so it invites pity rather than shame, where *derelict* makes it a matter for blame.

notes.gloss: completely and without qualification; used informally as intensifiers
notes.note: The adverb of *utter*: flat and absolute - it allows no remainder, and unlike *arrant* it supplies no sneer of its own.

notes.gloss: harmful to living things
notes.note: Formal and clinical, it records damage to living things as a finding, not a complaint, cooling what *hurtful* says plainly.

notes.gloss: occurring unexpectedly and requiring urgent action
notes.note: Flat and practical beside *explosive*: the unexpected counts only because it demands urgent action, not because it startles.

notes.gloss: not mixed with extraneous elements
notes.note: The flattest word here: it says nothing that does not belong is mixed in, and neither praises nor criticizes that.

notes.gloss: reduced to nothingness
notes.note: Formal and cold beside *blotted out*: the *-ed* ending points back to an act, and nothing is left, not something hidden.

notes.gloss: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
notes.note: The *-est* ending does the work: it does not just call the person dear but sets them above everyone else.

notes.gloss: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
notes.note: Points at the mind as what is doing the work, not at whether its results are sound: a label, not a judgment.

notes.gloss: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
notes.note: Heavier than *constant*, because it adds being reliable: the firmness becomes something others can lean on.

notes.gloss: of metal e.g.
notes.note: Damage to the shape across the whole thing, not along one line - more thorough than *bent*, but judging just as little.

notes.gloss: someone who supports or champions something
notes.note: Approving, but the praise is for backing or speaking up for something, not for getting a person out of trouble.

notes.gloss: not brought to the desired final state
notes.note: Faintly disapproving: it measures the thing against the final state that was wanted, so it records falling short, not just a stage.

notes.gloss: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
notes.note: Formal and cool: it notes the reaching for recognition or advancement without judging it, where *aspiring* sounds warm.

notes.gloss: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
notes.note: The plainest, most forgiving word: it names the fault without picturing the head, and leaves room for fondness that *airheaded* shuts out.

notes.gloss: (of an animal) having no home or having wandered away from home
notes.note: Pity and a touch of nuisance at once, for an animal with no home or one that has wandered off.

notes.gloss: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
notes.note: The *-ing* form keeps the careless speed going on as an activity, not the single finished act *rush* names.

notes.gloss: eager to investigate and learn or learn more (sometimes about others' concerns)
notes.note: Approves of the eager mind, a little wary of the manner - the meaning allows both.

notes.gloss: filled with melancholy and despondency
notes.note: Spreads rather than strikes - the low, hopeless mood hangs around the person like settled weather, where *deflated* feels like one blow.

notes.gloss: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
notes.note: The mildest word here for faking it: the fault is the wish to look good, where *pretence* blames the falseness itself.

notes.gloss: capable of arousing sexual desire
notes.note: Enjoys the sexual desire the thing stirs, where the cooler *sexually attractive* only reports it.

notes.gloss: indicate by marking trees with blazes
notes.note: Literal where *mark* is not: the sign is really cut into trees, so the word names its method and judges nothing.

notes.gloss: causing fear or anxiety by threatening great harm
notes.note: The flattest word here: it insists the threatened harm is real, without making its force dramatic as *severe* does.

notes.gloss: deserving blame
notes.note: The mildest blame word: it says where blame lies but not what kind of act it was, while *guilty* calls the act wrong.

notes.gloss: an adulterous woman; a woman who has an ongoing extramarital sexual relationship with a man
notes.note: The blame is built into the word: a woman in an ongoing affair outside marriage, where *concubine* names only a shared household.

notes.gloss: highly cultured or educated
notes.note: The same claim to being highly cultured as *highbrow*, but the *-ed* ending makes it sit heavier and stiffer.

notes.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
notes.note: The barest word here, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the deceit unsaid, where *pretence* puts the trick on show.

notes.gloss: made of inferior workmanship and materials
notes.note: Cheapness trying to look flashy - which is what makes it worth scorn, not merely poor.

notes.gloss: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
notes.note: Formal to the point of stiffness - the same praise as *approving*, raised into official language.

notes.gloss: growing old
notes.note: Clinical and detached: the same growing old as *aging*, in a style that feels nothing about it.

notes.gloss: having lost freshness through passage of time
notes.note: Understated, almost a gentler way to say *stale*: it notes only that time has passed and taken the freshness with it.

notes.gloss: having the surface exposed and painful
notes.note: Reports pain where the jagged-edge words report shape: the covering is gone, leaving what lies under it exposed and stinging.

notes.gloss: giving or spending with reluctance
notes.note: A gentler word for stinginess, softening it into just being *close* with money.

notes.gloss: lacking strength or vigor
notes.note: Harsher than *faint*: the lack invites pity, and the pity slides into a judgement that it could never be enough.

notes.gloss: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
notes.note: The most abstract and academic of the set, naming mind-work in a high style where *mental* stays flat.

notes.gloss: formal or perfunctory politeness
notes.note: The lowest here: politeness as outward form, done correctly or gone through without interest, so it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.

notes.gloss: unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)
notes.note: Here a fault, not a virtue: self-esteem grown too big and past all reason, serious enough to be one of the deadly sins.

notes.gloss: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
notes.note: The shorter form reads as a state the thing is now in, where *burned* reports what happened to it.

notes.gloss: knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress
notes.note: Mild approval for the knack of heading off embarrassment or distress, a plain quality where *discretion* sounds like a virtue you are praised for.

notes.gloss: lacking in schooling
notes.note: Mild, almost taking the blame off the person: the lack is in the schooling they never had, not in their mind.

notes.gloss: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
notes.note: Not being there when relied on, whether by proving unreliable or by walking away, but framed as a lapse rather than a wrong.

notes.gloss: radically new or original
notes.note: Approval for newness pushed to its edge, where breaking with what came before is everything - a bigger claim than *fresh* makes.

notes.gloss: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
notes.note: Turns the demand on everything you have into an invitation to rise to it, where *problematic* treats the demand as a fault.

notes.gloss: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
notes.note: Puts the weight of a legal charge behind blame that is moral, not legal - an outcry where *condemnable* is a ruling.

notes.gloss: capable of producing violent emotion or arousing controversy
notes.note: A load waiting to go off: violent feeling or controversy stored up, where *inflammatory* is already at work.

notes.gloss: destroyed financially
notes.note: Formal, naming the poverty left behind rather than the break itself - a settled state, where *broken* sounds like a moment.

notes.gloss: brought low in spirit
notes.note: Same sense as *chopfallen*, and like it stresses the fall: a spirit brought down from a height, not one always low.

notes.gloss: marked by extreme lack of restraint or control
notes.note: Names how extreme the missing restraint is without colouring it, and leans negative only because that lack is extreme rather than partial.

notes.gloss: (of persons) taken advantage of
notes.note: Informal, and seen from the sufferer's side: the person visibly feels the wrong, where *ill-used* and *exploited* only report it.

notes.gloss: worn and broken down by hard use
notes.note: Scornful and vivid - it adds filth to simple wear and tear.

notes.gloss: likely to be affected by something
notes.note: Names exposure, not outcome: nothing has landed yet, the thing just stands open to it, unlike every struck-and-overcome word here.

notes.gloss: capable of happening or existing
notes.note: The bare minimum: it says only that the thing is not ruled out, promising nothing about anyone managing to do it.

notes.gloss: causing dejection
notes.note: Gloom mixed with scorn: what it names is not just depressing but pathetic, which *gloomy* never suggests.

notes.gloss: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
notes.note: Informal and dismissive — the strangeness is treated as too lightweight to be taken seriously.

notes.gloss: mentally or physically infirm with age
notes.note: Informal and blunt - the same weakness from age as *doddering*, in a word too jokey to leave the person any dignity.

notes.gloss: the act of giving a false appearance
notes.note: The flat, general word for putting up a false front, without the wish to impress that softens *appearance*; British spelling.

notes.gloss: based on sound reasoning or evidence
notes.note: The coolest, most reluctant approval here: the reasoning can be defended, where *well-founded* says its grounds are solid.

notes.gloss: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
notes.note: Not just distance but too much: an opinion or action pushed past what its own position would allow, where *far* stays neutral.

notes.gloss: not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity, or significance
notes.note: A flat denial, not a complaint: the two are not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity or significance.

notes.gloss: having confidence restored; freed from anxiety
notes.note: The settled calm of confidence handed back as worry lifts, where the rest of the family never mentions it having been shaken.

notes.gloss: involving risk or danger
notes.note: Formal and classifying - it records danger as a feature to be measured, cooler than *risky*, which sounds like advice.

notes.gloss: needing no explanation
notes.note: The thing explains itself, so nothing needs to be added - where *obvious* only says it is easy to grasp.

notes.gloss: unable to function; without help
notes.note: Two failures at once, unable to function and no help at hand, so it sounds like a plea, not *hopeless*'s verdict.

notes.gloss: pertaining to unconventional choices
notes.note: Treats the break from the usual as something chosen, and a choice can be described without being condemned.

notes.gloss: strikingly different; tending to contrast
notes.note: The same striking difference as *contrasting*, but framed as a quality a thing has rather than an effect it produces.

notes.gloss: moving at very high speed
notes.note: The danger is in the picture, not a verdict: a pace fast enough to break a neck, which can sound thrilling or reckless.

notes.gloss: suggesting connivance
notes.note: The British spelling of *cozy*, with the same accusation of secret cooperation in wrongdoing - warmth named in order to be distrusted.

notes.gloss: showing utter resignation or hopelessness
notes.note: Simply “not hopeful”: the same utter resignation or hopelessness as *abject*, but without the scorn, saying less than it means.

notes.gloss: an inclination to favor one group or view or opinion over alternatives
notes.note: The plain name for leaning toward one side: the scales are tipped, but unlike *prejudice* it does not say the case is closed.

notes.gloss: having precedence (especially because of longer service)
notes.note: Formal and procedural: it turns seniority into a right to go first, a right *senior* leaves unsaid.

notes.gloss: not modified or restricted by reservations
notes.note: A blunt single syllable that shuts the door on reservations, where *categorical* refuses them like a formal declaration.

notes.gloss: guilty of murder or bloodshed
notes.note: The most serious here: guilt for killing, which the word treats as a stain carried rather than a charge answered.

notes.gloss: diverging from another or from a standard
notes.note: Makes difference a moving apart - from another thing or from a standard - where *disparate* simply finds two things unlike.

notes.gloss: not created for a particular occasion
notes.note: Describes without judging: it marks a thing as kept ready for whatever comes, instead of set up for one occasion.

notes.gloss: (of persons) dangerously reckless or violent as from urgency or despair
notes.note: Said of a person, not a situation: past caution and likely to turn violent; the despair behind it does not soften the warning.

notes.gloss: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
notes.note: Makes the quality total as if it were a finished achievement, and that mismatch gives it a dry humour *utter* lacks.

notes.gloss: natural and unstudied
notes.note: Approving, and sounds like easy talk: it praises being natural rather than put on, where *informal* only notes what is missing.

notes.gloss: more desirable than another
notes.note: A comparison and nothing more - it rates one thing above another without claiming either is wanted much at all.

notes.gloss: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
notes.note: Clinical - a softer word, chosen to avoid saying *dirty*.

notes.gloss: beyond a norm in opinion or actions
notes.note: Just a position: it puts an opinion or action past the norm and leaves the judging to others, where *outrageous* is all judgement.

notes.gloss: easily seen or detected
notes.note: Almost technical in feel: something a look or a test turns up, where *perceptible* is something the senses take in.

notes.gloss: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
notes.note: The most deliberate of these, spelling out that nothing was mixed in to weaken the quality, where *pure* says it in a breath.

notes.gloss: not used to good advantage
notes.note: Says that value came to nothing without pointing at anyone to blame, which is what *squandered* adds.

notes.gloss: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
notes.note: The same verdict as *retributive*, but more mechanical - it sounds like the machinery of paying back, not the principle behind it.

notes.gloss: requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
notes.note: Plain and calm - it names how much is asked without judging whether that is fair, where *hard-to-please* has already found someone guilty.

notes.gloss: sufficiently interesting to be reported in a newspaper
notes.note: A bar to clear, not a compliment: it asks whether something has enough interest to report, where *interesting* describes the pull itself.

notes.gloss: free from control or responsibility
notes.note: Simply states where someone stands - there is no one to answer to, and the person is not judged for it.

notes.gloss: morally objectionable behavior
notes.note: Condemns the same conduct with preachy relish, as if the wrong were knowingly enjoyed, not just done: more vivid than the bare *evil*.

notes.gloss: exaggeratedly proper
notes.note: Scornful: being too proper is taken as smugness, correct behaviour shown off as a mark of being better than others.

notes.gloss: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
notes.note: Leans hardest here on the very positive use: the trait does not just identify the thing, it raises it above others.

notes.gloss: in a state of sulky dissatisfaction
notes.note: Makes light of the complaint - the grumpy tone turns it into a mere mood, brushed aside along with the person complaining.

notes.gloss: no longer in use
notes.note: States the plain fact of non-use and leaves the reason alone.

notes.gloss: of or like a feeble old woman
notes.note: Formal-sounding but withering, covering both being a feeble old woman and merely being like one; the scorn is in the word itself.

notes.gloss: suggesting connivance
notes.note: Hints at wrongdoing - the closeness is treated as secret cooperation, so the word's comfortable warmth becomes the accusation.

notes.gloss: beguiling but harmful
notes.note: The warning is in the pairing: the charm is real and is exactly what hides the harm, where *corrupting* names the damage openly.

notes.gloss: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
notes.note: Coarse and total - a tangle or dead stop treated as a mess someone made and must answer for; the harshest word here.

notes.gloss: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
notes.note: The coldest of the three: the person is a thing picked up for dirty or merely unpleasant jobs, valued only for being used.

notes.gloss: having a defect
notes.note: Ordinary and fixable - it finds a fault to be put right rather than writing the thing off the way *defective* does.

notes.gloss: being in or verging on a state of crisis or emergency
notes.note: Marks the tipping point, the moment things break one way or the other - cooler and more clinical than *grave*.

notes.gloss: worthy of the greatest honor or distinction
notes.note: Goes past granting honor to set its subject at the very top of it, where *honorable* only confirms the honor is deserved.

notes.gloss: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
notes.note: Formal - it describes what a thing does to the people who see it, where *amazing* simply cries out.

notes.gloss: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
notes.note: Milder than *divine* and *elysian*: it credits the excellence to something breathed in from outside, but names no gods.

notes.gloss: having concealed difficulty
notes.note: Warns of a trap - the difficulty stays hidden until you are into it, so the thing is harder than it looks.

notes.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
notes.note: British spelling of the same misleading surface: a respectable tint lent to something so it passes, only a tint, where *disguise* covers.

notes.gloss: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
notes.note: Condemns the person themselves as something another made and can aim at any unpleasant or dishonest job, where *tool* condemns only their usefulness.

notes.gloss: completely wanting or lacking
notes.note: Light and quietly joking - a complete lack made to sound free of blame, the opposite feeling from *destitute*.

notes.gloss: marked by high spirits or excitement
notes.note: The same flash said in a smaller, prettier way - decorative where *scintillating* is dazzling.

notes.gloss: filled with melancholy and despondency
notes.note: Names the loss rather than the mood - the spirit has been drained out, which comes across as emptiness beside *gloomy*'s heaviness.

notes.gloss: showing or experiencing dissatisfaction or restless longing
notes.note: Covers dissatisfaction or restless longing like *discontented*, but reads as a fixed state where *discontented* allows a passing mood.

notes.gloss: marked by practical hardheaded intelligence
notes.note: Formal praise for judgement that sees through a situation, carrying more weight than *sharp*, which praises speed instead.

notes.gloss: (of sound or color) free from anything that dulls or dims
notes.note: Praises a sound or colour that nothing dulls or dims - brightness is the point, not the lack of dirt that *clean* marks.

notes.gloss: capable of being attained or accomplished
notes.note: Informal and homely, it makes the thing sound simply within arm's length, where *attainable* makes the reach sound impressive.

notes.gloss: mentally perceptive and responsive
notes.note: Shows a sharp, noticing mind as full of life - stirred and answering, rather than simply watchful.

notes.gloss: characterized by physical or psychological maltreatment
notes.note: The heaviest word here, since the harm is a person treated cruelly in body or mind, not the general damage *harmful* allows.

notes.gloss: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
notes.note: The desire it raises may be one you argue with yourself over, so the pull feels like pressure, not *enticing*'s clean invitation.

notes.gloss: shockingly brutal or cruel
notes.note: Formal and bookish where *atrocious* is loud: the same charge of brutality, made coldly.

notes.gloss: having or appealing to those having worldly knowledge and refinement and savoir-faire
notes.note: Praises worldly knowledge and refinement together, and can describe things made for such people, not just the people - which *urbane* cannot.

notes.gloss: without or almost without wind
notes.note: A bare measure - no wind, or almost none - without the approval *tranquil* carries.

notes.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
notes.note: The ordinary *-ed* form for that same ragged tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays curt.

notes.gloss: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
notes.note: The highest praise - skill carried to its finish with nothing left to add, far above the everyday *proficient*.

notes.gloss: a woman's virtue or chastity
notes.note: Makes a woman's chastity her standing, something she is credited with and can be stripped of, where *virtue* only calls it moral.

notes.gloss: helping to restore to good condition
notes.note: The same approving sense of repair as *reconstructive*, but the longer, more formal word makes the help sound ongoing, not a single fix.

notes.gloss: not perceived or commented on
notes.note: Leans the other way from *unperceived*: the thing may well have been seen, and the point is that nothing was said of it.

notes.gloss: causing dejection
notes.note: Informal, and it colours the mood without condemning the thing, where *dismal* passes judgement on it.

notes.gloss: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
notes.note: Formal, and its cool tone sits strangely on an eagerness for bloodshed, condemning from a distance where *bloodthirsty* condemns close up.

notes.gloss: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
notes.note: Informal and dry: a big excess becomes a grumble, where *outrageous* turns the same excess into a protest.

notes.gloss: lacking consistency
notes.note: The mildest of these - it notes variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

notes.gloss: inviting cuddling or hugging
notes.note: Soft, casual and physical: it charms by asking to be cuddled or hugged, not by a good nature as in *sweet*.

notes.gloss: a person who loves someone or is loved by someone
notes.note: Works from either side: the one who loves or the one who is loved, stating the relation rather than acting it out.

notes.gloss: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
notes.note: Praises a place for feeling like home and putting you at ease, where *cozy* praises its warmth.

notes.gloss: (of fabrics and paper) grown dark in color over time
notes.note: The only word here about what time does to the colour of cloth or paper, not to a life, and it judges nothing.

notes.gloss: (of children and animals) young, immature
notes.note: The warmth is in the smallness: calling a child or young animal little makes it lovable, where *small* only measures.
